questions.question: A particle has position x(t)=t^3-6t^2+9t (SI units) for 0<=t<=5 s. What total distance does it travel?
questions.explanation: Velocity v=dx/dt=3(t-1)(t-3), so turning points are t=1,3 s. Positions are x(0)=0, x(1)=4, x(3)=0, x(5)=20 m. Total distance=|4-0|+|0-4|+|20-0|=28 m.

questions.question: A projectile is launched with speed 20 m/s and reaches a maximum height of 15 m. Taking g=10 m/s^2 and equal launch/landing levels, its range is
questions.explanation: H=u_y^2/(2g) gives u_y=sqrt(300)=10sqrt(3) m/s. Since u^2=u_x^2+u_y^2, u_x=10 m/s. Flight time=2u_y/g=2sqrt(3) s, hence R=u_x T=20sqrt(3) m.

questions.question: A river is 120 m wide. A boat's speed relative to water is 5 m/s and the current is 3 m/s. If it is aimed perpendicular to the bank to minimize crossing time, the crossing time is
questions.explanation: For minimum time the full boat speed contributes across the river. The across-river component is 5 m/s, so t=120/5=24 s. The current changes the downstream drift, not the crossing time.

questions.question: A particle moves along x(t)=2t^3-9t^2+12t. Its acceleration at t=2 s is
questions.explanation: Differentiate twice: v=6t^2-18t+12 and a=12t-18. At t=2 s, a=24-18=6 m/s^2.

questions.question: Particle A follows x_A=t^2+2t and particle B follows x_B=24-3t (SI units). They meet again at positive time
questions.explanation: Set positions equal: t^2+2t=24-3t, so t^2+5t-24=0=(t+8)(t-3). The physically relevant root is t=3 s.

questions.question: A particle moves in a circle of radius 5 m at constant speed 10 m/s. The magnitude of its acceleration is
questions.explanation: For uniform circular motion, a=v^2/r. Substituting v=10 m/s and r=5 m gives a=100/5=20 m/s^2, directed toward the centre.

questions.question: A projectile is launched at 25 m/s at 53 degrees above horizontal. Use sin53=0.8, cos53=0.6 and g=10 m/s^2. Its horizontal range is
questions.explanation: The components are u_x=25(0.6)=15 m/s and u_y=25(0.8)=20 m/s. Flight time=2u_y/g=4 s, so R=u_xT=15(4)=60 m.

questions.question: For a particle moving in a plane, the velocity and acceleration at an instant are v=3i+4j and a=-4i+3j in SI units. The instantaneous rate of change of speed is
questions.explanation: The rate of change of speed is the tangential component a_t=(v·a)/|v|. Here v·a=3(-4)+4(3)=0, so the acceleration is perpendicular to velocity and the speed is instantaneously unchanged.

questions.question: A projectile is fired horizontally at 20 m/s from a 45 m high cliff. Take g=10 m/s^2. Find the horizontal distance travelled before hitting the ground, in metres.
questions.explanation: Vertical motion gives 45=(1/2)10t^2, hence t=3 s. Horizontal velocity remains 20 m/s, so range from the cliff edge is x=20(3)=60 m.

questions.question: For x(t)=t^3-3t^2-9t, determine the time in seconds at which acceleration is zero for t>=0.
questions.explanation: Differentiate: v=3t^2-6t-9 and a=6t-6. Setting a=0 gives t=1 s.

questions.question: A particle's velocity is v(t)=2t-4 m/s for 0<=t<=5 s. Find its total distance in metres.
questions.explanation: Velocity changes sign at t=2 s. From 0 to 2 s, the negative triangular area has magnitude (1/2)(2)(4)=4 m. From 2 to 5 s, the positive triangular area is (1/2)(3)(6)=9 m. Total distance=4+9=13 m.

questions.question: A particle starts with velocity 2 m/s and has acceleration a(t)=6t-4 m/s^2. Find its velocity at t=3 s.
questions.explanation: Integrate acceleration: v(t)=2+integral_0^t(6u-4)du=2+3t^2-4t. At t=3 s, v=2+27-12=17 m/s.

questions.question: A body moves at speed 12 m/s along a circle of radius 9 m. Find its centripetal acceleration in m/s^2.
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration a_c=v^2/r=12^2/9=144/9=16 m/s^2.

questions.question: The position of a particle is x=4t^2-2t metres. Find its displacement from t=0 to t=3 s, in metres.
questions.explanation: Displacement=x(3)-x(0)=[4(9)-6]-0=36-6=30 m. Displacement is signed; no turning-point analysis is needed for this question.

questions.question: Particle A has x_A=t^2+2t and particle B has x_B=50-3t, with positions in metres and time in seconds. At what positive time do they meet?
questions.explanation: Equating positions gives t^2+2t=50-3t, or t^2+5t-50=0=(t+10)(t-5). The positive solution is 5 s.

questions.question: A particle has velocity v=6t-12 m/s. At what time in seconds is its velocity zero?
questions.explanation: Set v=0: 6t-12=0, so t=2 s.

questions.question: A 4 kg block slides down a rough 37-degree incline. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.25; take g=10 m/s^2, sin37=0.6 and cos37=0.8. Its acceleration down the plane is
questions.explanation: Down-slope gravity is mg sin37=24 N. Normal reaction is mg cos37=32 N, giving friction mu N=8 N up-slope. Net force=16 N, so a=16/4=4 m/s^2.

questions.question: Masses 3 kg and 2 kg are connected by a light string over a frictionless pulley. Taking g=10 m/s^2, the string tension is
questions.explanation: For an Atwood machine, a=(3-2)g/(3+2)=2 m/s^2. For the heavier mass, 30-T=3(2), hence T=24 N.

questions.question: A 2 kg block on a smooth horizontal surface is pulled by a horizontal force F(t)=6+2t N, starting from rest at t=0. Its speed at t=3 s is
questions.explanation: Impulse J=integral_0^3(6+2t)dt=18+9=27 N s. Since J=m delta-v and initial speed is zero, v=27/2=13.5 m/s.

questions.question: A body moves along x under force F(x)=3x^2 N from x=0 to x=2 m. The work done is
questions.explanation: Work is the integral of force over displacement: W=integral_0^2 3x^2 dx=[x^3]_0^2=8 J.

questions.question: A car travels around a flat circular track of radius r at speed v. If the coefficient of static friction is mu, the maximum speed without skidding is
questions.explanation: Static friction provides the centripetal force: mu mg >= mv^2/r. Cancelling m and rearranging gives v_max=sqrt(mu g r).

questions.question: A force F=(2x)i+(3y)j N acts from (0,0) to (2,1) m. Its work along any path joining the endpoints is
questions.explanation: The force is conservative because partial F_x/partial y=partial F_y/partial x=0. A potential-work integral gives W=integral 2x dx + integral 3y dy = [x^2]_0^2 + [(3/2)y^2]_0^1 =4+1.5=5.5 J.

questions.question: A 2 kg block moves right at 10 m/s on a rough horizontal surface with mu_k=0.5. Taking g=10 m/s^2, the stopping distance is
questions.explanation: Kinetic friction gives constant deceleration a=mu g=5 m/s^2. From v_f^2=v_i^2-2ad, 0=100-10d, so d=10 m.

questions.question: A 5 kg block is lifted vertically upward at constant speed 2 m/s. Taking g=10 m/s^2, the power delivered by the lifting force is
questions.explanation: Constant speed means lifting force equals mg=50 N. Power P=Fv=50(2)=100 W.

questions.question: A 3 kg block initially at rest is acted on by a constant net force of 12 N for 5 s. Find its final speed in m/s.
questions.explanation: Newton's second law gives a=F/m=12/3=4 m/s^2. Starting from rest, v=at=4(5)=20 m/s.

questions.question: A spring of force constant 200 N/m is compressed by 0.3 m. Find the stored elastic potential energy in joules.
A 2 kg body initially at rest falls through 5 m in vacuum. Take g=10 m/s^2. Find its kinetic energy just before impact, in joules.
questions.explanation: Mechanical energy is conserved. Lost gravitational potential energy mgh=2(10)(5)=100 J becomes kinetic energy.

questions.question: A motor pulls a load with a constant force of 40 N at a steady speed of 3 m/s. Find its mechanical output power in watts.
questions.explanation: For force parallel to velocity, P=Fv=40(3)=120 W.

questions.question: A 1 kg block moving at 8 m/s is brought to rest by a constant opposing force over 4 m. Find the magnitude of the force in newtons.
questions.explanation: Work-energy theorem gives Fd=initial kinetic energy: F(4)=(1/2)(1)(8^2)=32 J. Thus F=8 N.

questions.question: A 4 kg block is pulled 6 m on a horizontal surface by a 30 N horizontal force. Friction is 10 N. Find the net work in joules.
questions.explanation: Net force along displacement is 30-10=20 N. Net work=(20)(6)=120 J; equivalently, applied work 180 J minus friction work 60 J.

questions.question: A 2 kg block is attached to a spring of constant 50 N/m. It is released from rest from x=0.4 m compression on a frictionless surface. Find its maximum speed in m/s.
questions.explanation: At equilibrium all spring energy becomes kinetic: (1/2)kx^2=(1/2)mv_max^2. Hence v_max=x sqrt(k/m)=0.4 sqrt(50/2)=0.4(5)=2 m/s.

questions.question: A 10 kg crate is pulled up a rough incline at constant speed. The incline is 30 degrees and friction is 20 N. Take g=10 m/s^2. Find the pulling force parallel to the plane, in newtons.
questions.explanation: Along the plane, gravity contributes mg sin30=10(10)(0.5)=50 N downhill and friction contributes 20 N downhill. Constant speed means zero net force, so the pull is 50+20=70 N.

questions.question: A solid cylinder rolls without slipping down a 30-degree incline. Its acceleration is (take g=10 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: For rolling, a=g sin(theta)/(1+I/(mR^2)). A solid cylinder has I=(1/2)mR^2, so a=10(1/2)/(1+1/2)=5/1.5=10/3 m/s^2.

questions.question: A 10 N force acts perpendicular to a 0.5 m lever arm about a fixed axis. The torque magnitude is
questions.explanation: Torque magnitude is tau=rF sin(theta). With theta=90 degrees, tau=0.5(10)=5 N m.

questions.question: A uniform rod of length 2 m is hinged at one end and released from horizontal. Its initial angular acceleration is (take g=10 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: About the hinge, initial torque=mg(L/2). The rod's moment of inertia is I=mL^2/3. Thus alpha=tau/I=[mgL/2]/[mL^2/3]=3g/(2L)=30/4=7.5 rad/s^2.

questions.question: Two equal masses m are at x=0 and x=4a; a third mass 3m is at x=2a. The centre of mass coordinate is
A ring and a solid disc have equal mass and radius and roll without slipping at the same centre-of-mass speed. Which has greater total kinetic energy?
options: Ring, with total energy 4/3 that of the disc
Disc, with total energy 4/3 that of the ring
Both have equal total kinetic energy
Ring, with twice the total kinetic energy of the disc
questions.explanation: For rolling without slipping, K=(1/2)Mv^2+(1/2)I(v^2/R^2). For a ring, I=MR^2, so K_ring=Mv^2. For a solid disc, I=(1/2)MR^2, so K_disc=(3/4)Mv^2. Therefore K_ring/K_disc=4/3.

questions.question: A rotating platform has moment of inertia I and angular speed omega. A person moves inward so the new moment of inertia is I/2, with negligible external torque. The new angular speed is
questions.explanation: Angular momentum is conserved: I omega=(I/2) omega_f, hence omega_f=2omega.

questions.question: A constant torque of 6 N m acts on a wheel through an angular displacement of 4 rad in the torque direction. Work done is
questions.explanation: For constant torque, rotational work W=tau Delta-theta=6(4)=24 J.

questions.question: A uniform disc has mass 2 kg and radius 0.5 m. The moment of inertia about its central axis is
questions.explanation: For a uniform disc about its symmetry axis, I=(1/2)MR^2=(1/2)(2)(0.25)=0.25 kg m^2.

questions.question: A 2 kg point mass moves at 3 m/s in a circle of radius 4 m. Find its angular momentum magnitude about the centre, in kg m^2/s.
questions.explanation: For a point mass moving tangentially, L=mvr=2(3)(4)=24 kg m^2/s.

questions.question: Two particles of masses 2 kg and 6 kg are at x=0 m and x=8 m. Find their centre of mass coordinate in metres.
A wheel with moment of inertia 4 kg m^2 experiences a net torque of 12 N m. Find its angular acceleration in rad/s^2.
questions.explanation: Rotational dynamics gives tau=I alpha, hence alpha=12/4=3 rad/s^2.

questions.question: A solid sphere of mass 5 kg and radius 0.5 m rolls without slipping at 2 m/s. Find its total kinetic energy in joules.
questions.explanation: For a solid sphere I=(2/5)MR^2 and omega=v/R. Total K=(1/2)Mv^2+(1/2)I omega^2=(1/2+1/5)Mv^2=(7/10)(5)(4)=14 J.

questions.question: A uniform rod of mass 3 kg and length 2 m rotates about its centre perpendicular to its length at 4 rad/s. Find its rotational kinetic energy in joules.
questions.explanation: For a uniform rod about its centre, I=ML^2/12=3(2^2)/12=1 kg m^2. Rotational kinetic energy=(1/2)I omega^2=(1/2)(1)(4^2)=8 J.

questions.question: A pulley of moment of inertia 2 kg m^2 has a string wound at radius 0.5 m. A tangential force of 8 N is applied. Find angular acceleration in rad/s^2.
questions.explanation: The applied torque is tau=FR=8(0.5)=4 N m. Angular acceleration alpha=tau/I=4/2=2 rad/s^2.

questions.question: A 2 kg mass moving at 5 m/s sticks to a stationary 3 kg mass in a one-dimensional collision. Find the speed after collision in m/s.
questions.explanation: Linear momentum is conserved: (2)(5)+(3)(0)=(2+3)v. Thus v=10/5=2 m/s.

questions.question: A uniform ring of mass 4 kg and radius 0.5 m rotates at 6 rad/s. Find its rotational kinetic energy in joules.
A satellite in a circular orbit of radius r around Earth has speed v. A satellite in orbit radius 4r has speed
questions.explanation: Circular orbital speed v=sqrt(GM/r). Replacing r by 4r gives v'=sqrt(GM/(4r))=v/2.

questions.question: At a height equal to Earth's radius above its surface, the gravitational acceleration is
questions.explanation: Height h=R gives distance from Earth's centre 2R. Since g(r)=GM/r^2, g'=GM/(2R)^2=g/4.

questions.question: A planet has the same mean density as Earth but twice Earth's radius. Its surface gravitational acceleration is
questions.explanation: For a uniform-density sphere, M=(4/3)pi rho R^3, so g=GM/R^2=(4/3)pi G rho R. Doubling R at fixed density doubles surface g.

questions.question: The gravitational field inside a uniform thin spherical shell is
questions.explanation: By the shell theorem, the net gravitational field at every interior point of a uniform thin spherical shell is zero. Its potential is constant inside, although not zero.

questions.question: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius r. Its total mechanical energy is
questions.explanation: For circular orbit, K=GMm/(2r) and U=-GMm/r. Therefore E=K+U=-GMm/(2r).

questions.question: Two equal masses M are separated by distance d. The gravitational potential at their midpoint, taking zero at infinity, is
questions.explanation: Each mass is d/2 from the midpoint, so each contributes gravitational potential -GM/(d/2)=-2GM/d. Potentials add algebraically, giving V=-4GM/d, option index 2.

questions.question: If a planet's orbital period around a star is T at orbital radius r, the period at radius 9r is
questions.explanation: Kepler's third law gives T^2 proportional to r^3. Therefore T'/T=(9)^(3/2)=27, so T'=27T.

questions.question: The escape speed from a planet is v_e. If its mass is unchanged but its radius doubles, the new escape speed is
questions.explanation: Escape speed v_e=sqrt(2GM/R). At radius 2R, v'_e=sqrt(2GM/(2R))=v_e/sqrt(2).

questions.question: At a distance 2R from a planet’s centre, gravitational acceleration is g/4. Express the acceleration in units of g/4.
questions.explanation: Outside the planet, g(r)=GM/r^2. At r=2R, g(r)=GM/(4R^2)=g/4, which is exactly 1 unit of g/4.

questions.question: A 500 kg satellite orbits a planet with GM=4.0 x 10^14 m^3/s^2 at radius 1.0 x 10^7 m. Find its orbital speed in km/s, rounded to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: v=sqrt(GM/r)=sqrt(4.0 x 10^14/10^7)=sqrt(4.0 x 10^7)=6324.9 m/s=6.325 km/s, which rounds to 6 km/s.

questions.question: A planet's surface gravity is 8 m/s^2 and radius is 2 x 10^6 m. Using v_e=sqrt(2gR), find escape speed in km/s to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: v_e=sqrt(2(8)(2 x 10^6))=sqrt(32 x 10^6)=5657 m/s=5.657 km/s, which rounds to 6 km/s.

questions.question: A 100 kg satellite is in a circular orbit of radius 2R around a planet of mass M. Write its kinetic energy as K=C GM/R. Find C.
questions.explanation: For a circular orbit, K=GMm/(2r). Here m=100 kg and r=2R, so K=GM(100)/(4R)=25 GM/R; hence C=25.

questions.question: A body is moved from a planet surface (radius R) to a height R above the surface. Find the increase in gravitational potential energy in units of GMm/(2R).
questions.explanation: Initial U_i=-GMm/R and final U_f=-GMm/(2R). Thus Delta-U=U_f-U_i=GMm/(2R), equal to 1 unit of GMm/(2R).

questions.question: Two masses 4 kg and 9 kg are separated by 2 m. Find the magnitude of their gravitational attraction in units of G, in N when SI units are used: F=(coefficient)G.
questions.explanation: Newton's law gives F=Gm_1m_2/r^2=G(4)(9)/2^2=9G. The coefficient is 9.

questions.question: A satellite's orbital radius is four times a second satellite's orbital radius around the same planet. If the inner satellite's period is 3 hours, find the outer satellite's period in hours.
questions.explanation: Kepler's law gives T proportional to r^(3/2). The period ratio is 4^(3/2)=8, so the outer period is 3(8)=24 hours.

questions.question: A planet has mass 4 x 10^24 kg and radius 2 x 10^6 m. Using G=6.67 x 10^-11 SI, estimate surface gravity to the nearest integer in m/s^2.

questions.question: A wire of length L, cross-sectional area A and Young's modulus Y is stretched by force F. Its extension is
questions.explanation: Young's modulus Y=(stress)/(strain)=(F/A)/(Delta L/L). Rearranging gives Delta L=FL/(AY).

questions.question: For a small sphere falling through a viscous fluid in the Stokes regime, terminal speed is proportional to
questions.explanation: At terminal speed, effective weight is balanced by Stokes drag 6 pi eta r v. The buoyancy-corrected weight scales as r^3, so v_t scales as r^3/r=r^2.

questions.question: An incompressible fluid flows steadily through a pipe whose area decreases from 8 cm^2 to 2 cm^2. If the speed in the wider section is 1.5 m/s, the speed in the narrower section is
questions.explanation: Continuity gives A_1v_1=A_2v_2. Hence v_2=(8/2)(1.5)=6 m/s.

questions.question: In a horizontal Venturi tube, water speed rises from 2 m/s to 6 m/s. Taking density 1000 kg/m^3 and neglecting viscosity, the pressure drop is
questions.explanation: Bernoulli gives p_1-p_2=(1/2)rho(v_2^2-v_1^2)=(1/2)(1000)(36-4)=16000 Pa=16 kPa, which is option index 1.

questions.question: A capillary of radius r shows a rise h for a liquid. If the radius is doubled while all liquid properties remain fixed, the rise becomes
questions.explanation: Capillary rise h=2T cos(theta)/(rho g r), so it is inversely proportional to radius. Doubling r halves h.

questions.question: A cube of density 600 kg/m^3 floats in a liquid of density 1000 kg/m^3. The fraction of its volume submerged is
questions.explanation: Floating equilibrium requires rho_liquid V_sub g=rho_cube V g. Thus V_sub/V=rho_cube/rho_liquid=600/1000=0.6.

questions.question: A material has bulk modulus 2 x 10^9 Pa. Under a uniform pressure increase of 1 x 10^6 Pa, the magnitude of its fractional volume change is
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus B=Delta p/(-Delta V/V). Therefore |Delta V|/V=Delta p/B=10^6/(2 x 10^9)=5 x 10^-4, which is option index 1.

questions.question: In a hydraulic lift, the small piston has area 2 cm^2 and the large piston has area 200 cm^2. If the input force is 50 N, the ideal output force is
questions.explanation: Pascal's law gives F_1/A_1=F_2/A_2. Thus F_2=50(200/2)=5000 N.

questions.question: A 2 m long wire of area 1 x 10^-6 m^2 and Young's modulus 2 x 10^11 Pa is stretched by 100 N. Find its extension in millimetres.
Water flows through a pipe with area 6 cm^2 at speed 4 m/s. Find the volume flow rate in cm^3/s.
questions.explanation: Volume flow rate Q=Av. In these units, Q=6 cm^2 x 400 cm/s=2400 cm^3/s.

questions.question: A liquid of density 1000 kg/m^3 is at depth 3 m. Taking g=10 m/s^2, find the gauge pressure in kPa.
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure p=rho gh=1000(10)(3)=30000 Pa=30 kPa.

questions.question: A spherical drop has radius 2 mm and surface tension 0.05 N/m. For a single liquid-air surface, find the excess pressure in pascals.
questions.explanation: For a liquid drop, excess pressure Delta p=2T/r=2(0.05)/(0.002)=50 Pa.

questions.question: For laminar flow through a cylindrical tube, the radius is doubled while pressure difference, length and viscosity stay fixed. By what factor does volume flow rate change?
questions.explanation: Poiseuille's law gives Q proportional to r^4. Doubling the radius multiplies flow rate by 2^4=16.

questions.question: A 4 m long wire extends by 2 mm under a certain load. Find the strain, expressed in units of 10^-4, i.e. enter strain x 10^4.
questions.explanation: Strain=Delta L/L=0.002/4=5 x 10^-4. Multiplying by 10^4 gives 5.

questions.question: A 2 m long wire extends by 1 mm under a tensile load. Find the strain multiplied by 10^6.
questions.explanation: Strain=Delta-L/L=(1 x 10^-3)/2=5 x 10^-4. Multiplying by 10^6 gives 500.

questions.question: A wire of length 2 m, cross-sectional area 1 x 10^-6 m^2 and Young’s modulus 2 x 10^11 Pa is stretched by 1000 N. Find its extension in millimetres.
questions.explanation: For axial extension, Delta-L=FL/(AY). Substitution gives Delta-L=(1000)(2)/[(1 x 10^-6)(2 x 10^11)]=2000/(2 x 10^5)=0.01 m=10 mm.

questions.question: A 200 g sample of water at 20 C is mixed with 100 g of water at 80 C in an insulated vessel. The final temperature is
questions.explanation: With equal specific heat and no heat loss, heat gained equals heat lost: 200(T-20)=100(80-T). Thus 300T=12000, giving T=40 C.

questions.question: A metal plate has a circular hole. When the plate is uniformly heated, the hole's radius
options: increases by the same fractional amount as the plate's length
increases by twice the fractional amount of area expansion
questions.explanation: Uniform expansion scales every linear dimension by 1+alpha Delta-T. The boundary of the hole expands just as if the hole were filled with the same material, so its radius increases by fractional amount alpha Delta-T.

questions.question: Two rods of equal length and area are joined end-to-end. Their thermal conductivities are k and 3k. At steady state, the ratio of temperature drops across the first and second rods is
questions.explanation: The heat current is equal through rods in series. For each rod Delta-T=H L/(kA), so temperature drop is inversely proportional to conductivity. Thus Delta-T_1:Delta-T_2=(1/k):(1/3k)=3:1.

questions.question: An ideal blackbody's absolute temperature is doubled. Its emitted power per unit area becomes
questions.explanation: Stefan-Boltzmann law gives emitted power per unit area proportional to T^4. Doubling T multiplies the power by 2^4=16.

questions.question: A completely constrained metal rod has Young's modulus Y and linear expansion coefficient alpha. If its temperature rises by Delta-T, the magnitude of thermal stress is
questions.explanation: Free thermal strain would be alpha Delta-T. Constraint forces total strain to zero, so mechanical strain has equal magnitude. Stress=Y times strain=Y alpha Delta-T.

questions.question: For an ideal gas, the root-mean-square molecular speed is proportional to
questions.explanation: From kinetic theory, (1/2)m v_rms^2=(3/2)k_B T. Hence v_rms=sqrt(3k_BT/m), proportional to sqrt(T) when absolute temperature is used.

questions.question: A body cools in surroundings at 20 C. At one instant its temperature is 80 C; a small later interval of 1 minute lowers it to 74 C. Under Newton's law of cooling, the instantaneous cooling rate at 80 C is approximately
questions.explanation: Newton's law gives cooling rate proportional to excess temperature. Over the short interval the excess falls from 60 C to 54 C, so the proportional fall is 10% per minute. The initial rate is approximately 0.10(60)=6 C/min.

questions.question: A 100 g ice sample at 0 C is completely melted by supplying heat. If latent heat of fusion is 334 J/g, the required heat is
questions.explanation: During melting the temperature stays at 0 C. Heat Q=mL_f=(100 g)(334 J/g)=33400 J=33.4 kJ.

questions.question: A slab has thickness 0.1 m, area 2 m^2 and conductivity 0.5 W/(m K). Its faces are maintained at temperatures differing by 10 K. The steady heat current is
questions.explanation: Conduction rate H=kA Delta-T/L=(0.5)(2)(10)/(0.1)=100 W.

questions.question: A 2 m metal rod has linear expansion coefficient 1 x 10^-5 K^-1. Find its expansion in millimetres for a 50 K rise.
questions.explanation: Delta-L=alpha L Delta-T=(1 x 10^-5)(2)(50)=1 x 10^-3 m=1 mm.

questions.question: A 0.5 kg block of a material with specific heat 400 J/(kg K) is heated by 6000 J with no phase change. Find its temperature rise in kelvin.
The temperature of a blackbody changes from 300 K to 600 K. By what integer factor does its emitted power increase?
questions.explanation: By Stefan-Boltzmann law P is proportional to T^4, hence P_2/P_1=(600/300)^4=2^4=16.

questions.question: A 140 g metal sample at 100 C is dropped into 100 g water at 20 C. Their common final temperature is 40 C. Taking water specific heat as 4.2 J/(g K), find the metal specific heat in J/(g K).
questions.explanation: Water gains Q_w=100(4.2)(40-20)=8400 J. Metal loses Q_m=140 c(100-40)=8400c J. Equating heat gained and lost gives 8400=8400c, hence c=1 J/(g K).

questions.question: A 1.25 m wire has alpha=2 x 10^-5 K^-1. Find its increase in length in millimetres for a 40 K rise.
questions.explanation: Delta-L=alpha L Delta-T=(2 x 10^-5)(1.25)(40)=1 x 10^-3 m=1 mm.

questions.question: A 250 g substance at its melting point receives 20 kJ and melts completely. Find its latent heat of fusion in kJ/kg.
questions.explanation: L=Q/m=20 kJ/0.25 kg=80 kJ/kg.

questions.question: A 1 kg water sample cools from 90 C to 40 C. Taking specific heat 4200 J/(kg K), find the heat released in kJ.
questions.explanation: Q=mc Delta-T=1(4200)(50)=210000 J=210 kJ released.

questions.question: One mole of a monatomic ideal gas is heated at constant pressure by 300 K. If R=8.31 J/(mol K), the work done by the gas is
questions.explanation: At constant pressure, W=P Delta-V=nR Delta-T. With n=1 and Delta-T=300 K, W=300R J.

questions.question: A Carnot engine operates between reservoirs at 500 K and 300 K. Its maximum efficiency is
questions.explanation: Carnot efficiency eta=1-T_c/T_h=1-300/500=0.4=40%.

questions.question: For a reversible isothermal expansion of an ideal gas from V to 2V, which expression equals work done by the gas?
questions.explanation: At constant temperature, P=nRT/V. Thus W=integral_V^2V P dV=nRT integral_V^2V dV/V=nRT ln(2).

questions.question: For an ideal gas undergoing an adiabatic process, the relation between pressure and volume is
questions.explanation: For a reversible adiabatic ideal-gas process, the first law with Q=0 combined with the ideal-gas equation gives PV^gamma=constant, where gamma=C_p/C_v.

questions.question: Using the convention Delta-U=Q-W, a gas absorbs 500 J heat and does 200 J work. Its internal energy change is
questions.explanation: The first law is Delta-U=Q-W. Here Q=+500 J and W=+200 J, so Delta-U=500-200=+300 J.

questions.question: For one complete cycle of a thermodynamic system returning to its initial state, the net change in internal energy is
options: equal to net heat always regardless of work sign
questions.explanation: Internal energy is a state function. Since the final state equals the initial state, Delta-U over a complete cycle is zero. The first law then gives net Q=net W.

questions.question: A gas completes a clockwise rectangular cycle on a P-V diagram, with pressure difference 2 x 10^5 Pa and volume difference 3 x 10^-3 m^3. The net work done per cycle is
questions.explanation: The net work in a closed P-V cycle is the enclosed area. For a rectangle, W=Delta-P Delta-V=(2 x 10^5)(3 x 10^-3)=600 J. Clockwise traversal means positive work by the gas.

questions.question: For an ideal gas, C_p-C_v equals
questions.explanation: Mayer's relation for one mole of an ideal gas is C_p-C_v=R, independent of the gas's degrees of freedom.

questions.question: A gas absorbs 800 J heat and its internal energy increases by 500 J. Using Delta-U=Q-W, find the work done by the gas in joules.
questions.explanation: Rearrange the first law: W=Q-Delta-U=800-500=300 J.

questions.question: An ideal gas expands isobarically at pressure 2 x 10^5 Pa from 1 litre to 4 litres. Find the work done in joules.
questions.explanation: W=P Delta-V. The volume change is 3 L=3 x 10^-3 m^3, so W=(2 x 10^5)(3 x 10^-3)=600 J.

questions.question: A monatomic ideal gas has 2 moles at temperature 300 K. Using R=8.31 J/(mol K), find its internal energy in joules.
questions.explanation: For a monatomic ideal gas U=(3/2)nRT=(3/2)(2)(8.31)(300)=7479 J.

questions.question: A Carnot refrigerator operates between 270 K and 300 K. Find its coefficient of performance, COP=T_c/(T_h-T_c).
One mole of ideal gas is heated at constant volume from 300 K to 400 K. For a monatomic gas and R=8.31 J/(mol K), find the heat supplied in joules rounded to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: At constant volume W=0, so Q=Delta-U=(3/2)nR Delta-T=(3/2)(8.31)(100)=1246.5 J, which rounds to 1247 J.

questions.question: An ideal gas undergoes an adiabatic process with gamma=5/3. Its initial temperature is 300 K and volume halves. Find the final temperature in kelvin rounded to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: For an adiabatic ideal gas, TV^(gamma-1)=constant. Thus T_f/T_i=(V_i/V_f)^(gamma-1)=2^(2/3)=1.5874. So T_f=300(1.5874)=476.2 K, approximately 476 K.

questions.question: A gas completes a clockwise rectangular P-V cycle of pressure width 4 x 10^4 Pa and volume width 5 x 10^-3 m^3. Find the net work done by the gas in joules.
questions.explanation: Net cyclic work equals the enclosed area: W=Delta-P Delta-V=(4 x 10^4)(5 x 10^-3)=200 J. Clockwise direction makes this work positive.

questions.question: For one mole of an ideal gas, C_v=3R/2. Find the value of 2C_p/R.
questions.explanation: Mayer relation gives C_p=C_v+R=(3/2)R+R=(5/2)R. Thus 2C_p/R=5.

questions.question: A 2 kg mass is attached to a spring of force constant 200 N/m on a frictionless surface. Its angular frequency is
questions.explanation: For a spring-mass oscillator omega=sqrt(k/m)=sqrt(200/2)=sqrt(100)=10 rad/s.

questions.question: A simple pendulum has period T on a planet with gravitational acceleration g. At the same location, if its length is increased by a factor of 4, its period becomes
questions.explanation: For small oscillations T=2pi sqrt(L/g). Quadrupling length multiplies the period by sqrt(4)=2.

questions.question: In SHM x=A cos(omega t), the speed when x=A/2 is
questions.explanation: Using v^2=omega^2(A^2-x^2), at x=A/2 we get v=omega sqrt(A^2-A^2/4)=sqrt(3)A omega/2.

questions.question: In a spring-mass SHM, the particle is at x=A/2 from equilibrium. The ratio of potential energy to total energy is
questions.explanation: Potential energy U=(1/2)kx^2 while total energy E=(1/2)kA^2. Thus U/E=x^2/A^2=(1/2)^2=1/4.

questions.question: Two ideal springs of constants k and 2k are connected in series. Their equivalent spring constant is
questions.explanation: For springs in series, 1/k_eq=1/k+1/(2k)=3/(2k), so k_eq=2k/3.

questions.question: Two ideal springs of constants k and 2k are connected in parallel and support a mass m. The angular frequency is
questions.explanation: Parallel spring constants add: k_eq=3k. Therefore omega=sqrt(k_eq/m)=sqrt(3k/m).

questions.question: A particle in SHM is at its mean position at t=0 and moves in the positive direction. Its displacement can be written
questions.explanation: At t=0 displacement must be zero. Positive velocity at t=0 selects x=A sin(omega t), since v=A omega cos(omega t)>0 initially.

questions.question: A spring-mass oscillator has amplitude A and total energy E. If its amplitude is doubled while the spring remains unchanged, its total energy becomes
questions.explanation: Total SHM energy E=(1/2)kA^2. Doubling A multiplies the energy by 2^2=4.

questions.question: A spring of constant 100 N/m supports a 4 kg mass in horizontal SHM. Find the period in seconds rounded to the nearest whole second. Use pi=3.14.
questions.explanation: T=2pi sqrt(m/k)=6.28 sqrt(4/100)=6.28(0.2)=1.256 s, which rounds to 1 s to the nearest whole second.

questions.question: A simple pendulum has length 1 m. Take g=pi^2 m/s^2. Find its small-oscillation period in seconds.
questions.explanation: T=2pi sqrt(L/g)=2pi sqrt(1/pi^2)=2 s.

questions.question: An SHM oscillator has angular frequency 5 rad/s and amplitude 0.4 m. Find its maximum acceleration magnitude in m/s^2.
questions.explanation: The maximum acceleration is a_max=omega^2 A=25(0.4)=10 m/s^2.

questions.question: A mass-spring oscillator has mass 1 kg and spring constant 64 N/m. Find its frequency in Hz using pi=3.14, rounded to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: omega=sqrt(k/m)=8 rad/s. Frequency f=omega/(2pi)=8/6.28=1.27 Hz, rounding to 1 Hz.

questions.question: A particle executes SHM with amplitude 5 cm and period 4 s. Find its maximum speed in cm/s, rounded to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: Maximum speed v_max=omega A=(2pi/T)A=(2pi/4)(5)=2.5pi=7.85 cm/s, which rounds to 8 cm/s.

questions.question: At a displacement x=3 cm, an SHM particle has amplitude 5 cm and speed 8 cm/s. Find its angular frequency in rad/s.
questions.explanation: From v^2=omega^2(A^2-x^2), omega=v/sqrt(A^2-x^2)=8/sqrt(25-9)=8/4=2 rad/s.

questions.question: A mass oscillates on a spring with period 2 s. How many complete oscillations does it make in 10 s?
questions.explanation: Number of complete periods is t/T=10/2=5.

questions.question: An oscillator has amplitude 0.2 m and spring constant 50 N/m. Find its total mechanical energy in joules.
A transverse wave travels on a string with tension 100 N and linear density 0.01 kg/m. Its speed is
questions.explanation: Wave speed on a stretched string is v=sqrt(T/mu)=sqrt(100/0.01)=sqrt(10000)=100 m/s.

questions.question: An open organ pipe has fundamental frequency 200 Hz. If its length is unchanged and one end is closed, the new fundamental frequency is
questions.explanation: An open pipe has f_open=v/(2L); a pipe closed at one end has f_closed=v/(4L). Thus f_closed=f_open/2=100 Hz.

questions.question: A source emitting 500 Hz sound moves toward a stationary observer at 20 m/s. If sound speed is 340 m/s, the observed frequency is approximately
questions.explanation: For an approaching source, f'=f v/(v-v_s)=500(340)/(340-20)=170000/320=531.25 Hz, approximately 531 Hz.

questions.question: Two tuning forks of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz are sounded together. The number of beats per second is
questions.explanation: Beat frequency is the absolute difference |f_1-f_2|=|260-256|=4 Hz.

questions.question: A string fixed at both ends has length L and wave speed v. Its third harmonic frequency is
questions.explanation: For a string fixed at both ends, f_n=nv/(2L). For n=3, f_3=3v/(2L).

questions.question: A sound source is isotropic and radiates power P uniformly. If distance from the source doubles, intensity becomes
questions.explanation: Intensity I=P/(4pi r^2), so doubling distance increases area by a factor of four and reduces intensity to I/4.

questions.question: A travelling wave is y=0.02 sin(4pi t-2pi x), with x in metres and t in seconds. Its speed is
questions.explanation: Compare with y=A sin(omega t-kx): omega=4pi rad/s and k=2pi rad/m. Wave speed omega/k=(4pi)/(2pi)=2 m/s.

questions.question: A pipe closed at one end has length L. Which harmonic is absent from its ideal resonance spectrum?
questions.explanation: A closed pipe supports odd harmonics f_n=(2n-1)v/(4L). Therefore even harmonics, including the second, are absent.

questions.question: A wave travels at 24 m/s and has frequency 6 Hz. Find its wavelength in metres.
questions.explanation: Wave relation v=f lambda gives lambda=v/f=24/6=4 m.

questions.question: An echo is heard 2 seconds after a sound pulse is emitted. If sound speed is 340 m/s, find the distance to the reflecting wall in metres.
questions.explanation: The sound travels to the wall and back, so 2d=vt=340(2)=680 m. Hence d=340 m.

questions.question: A string of length 1.5 m is fixed at both ends. If wave speed is 120 m/s, find its fundamental frequency in Hz.
questions.explanation: For the fundamental, lambda_1=2L=3 m. Thus f_1=v/lambda=120/3=40 Hz.

questions.question: Two coherent waves of equal amplitude have path difference lambda/2 at a point. Their phase difference in units of pi radians is
questions.explanation: Phase difference Delta-phi=2pi(Delta-x/lambda)=2pi(1/2)=pi. In units of pi radians, the answer is 1.

questions.question: A sound has intensity 100 times the reference intensity I_0. Find its sound level in decibels, using beta=10 log10(I/I_0).
A stationary source emits 680 Hz sound. An observer moves directly toward it at 10 m/s; sound speed is 340 m/s. Find observed frequency in Hz.
questions.explanation: For a moving observer approaching a stationary source, f'=f(v+v_o)/v=680(340+10)/340=680(350/340)=700 Hz.

questions.question: A wave has angular frequency 20 rad/s and wave number 5 rad/m. Find the wave speed in m/s.
questions.explanation: Wave speed is v=omega/k=20/5=4 m/s.

questions.question: Two sound waves of frequencies 440 Hz and 446 Hz are superposed. Find the number of beats per second.
questions.explanation: Beat frequency is |446-440|=6 Hz.

questions.question: Two charges +q and +4q are separated by distance d. The point between them where the net electric field is zero is at distance from +q equal to
questions.explanation: Between like charges their fields oppose. Set kq/x^2=k(4q)/(d-x)^2. Thus (d-x)=2x, giving x=d/3 from +q.

questions.question: The electric field inside a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium is
questions.explanation: Free charges in a conductor redistribute until the electrostatic field within the conducting material vanishes; otherwise charges would continue to move.

questions.question: Two point charges q and 2q are separated by r. Their electrostatic potential energy is U. If separation becomes 2r, the new potential energy is
questions.explanation: Potential energy of two point charges is U=kq_1q_2/r. Doubling r halves U, including its sign.

questions.question: Capacitors C and 2C are connected in series. Their equivalent capacitance is
questions.explanation: For series capacitors, 1/C_eq=1/C+1/(2C)=3/(2C). Therefore C_eq=2C/3.

questions.question: A dielectric of relative permittivity K is inserted fully into an isolated charged capacitor. The stored electrostatic energy becomes
questions.explanation: For an isolated capacitor, charge Q remains fixed. Since C increases to KC, energy U=Q^2/(2C) decreases to U/K.

questions.question: An electric dipole of moment p is placed in a uniform electric field E at angle theta. The torque magnitude is
questions.explanation: The dipole torque is vector tau=p x E, so its magnitude is pE sin(theta).

questions.question: The electric flux through a closed surface enclosing net charge Q is
questions.explanation: Gauss's law states integral E·dA=Q_enclosed/epsilon_0. The total flux depends on enclosed net charge, not on the surface shape.

questions.question: A parallel-plate capacitor is connected to a battery. If plate separation is doubled without changing the area, its capacitance and stored energy behave as
questions.explanation: C=epsilon_0 A/d, so doubling d halves C. The battery fixes V, and U=(1/2)CV^2, so stored energy also halves.

questions.question: Two charges 2 microcoulomb and 5 microcoulomb are separated by 0.1 m in vacuum. Using k=9 x 10^9 N m^2/C^2, find the force magnitude in newtons.
A charge of 5 microcoulomb is placed in an electric field of 2 x 10^6 N/C. Find the force magnitude in newtons.
A parallel-plate capacitor has area 0.02 m^2 and separation 1 mm. Using epsilon_0=8.85 x 10^-12 F/m, find its capacitance in pF, rounded to the nearest integer.
A 4 microfarad capacitor is charged to 10 V. Find its stored energy in units of 0.1 millijoule.
An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 100 V. Its kinetic energy gain in eV is
questions.explanation: A charge of magnitude e accelerated through potential difference V gains energy eV. In electron-volts, the numerical value is the voltage in volts, hence 100 eV.

questions.question: A point charge 2 microcoulomb is at the origin. Find the electric potential at a point 3 m away in kV, using k=9 x 10^9 SI.
Two identical 6 microfarad capacitors are connected in parallel across a 12 V battery. Find the total charge supplied by the battery in microcoulombs.
questions.explanation: Parallel capacitances add: C_eq=12 microfarad. Total charge Q=C_eq V=12(12)=144 microcoulomb.

questions.question: A charge q experiences force 12 N in a uniform electric field of 3 N/C. Find the magnitude of q in coulombs.
questions.explanation: From F=|q|E, |q|=F/E=12/3=4 C.

questions.question: A 6 ohm resistor and a 3 ohm resistor are connected in parallel across an ideal 12 V battery. The total current supplied is
questions.explanation: The equivalent resistance is 1/R_eq=1/6+1/3=1/2, hence R_eq=2 ohm. The battery current is I=V/R_eq=12/2=6 A.

questions.question: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance 1 ohm is connected to a 5 ohm external resistor. The terminal voltage is
questions.explanation: The current is I=E/(R+r)=12/(5+1)=2 A. Terminal voltage across the load is IR=2(5)=10 V, equal to E-Ir.

questions.question: At a junction, currents 2 A and 5 A enter while current I leaves. By Kirchhoff's junction law, I is
questions.explanation: Charge conservation requires total current entering to equal total current leaving. Thus I=2+5=7 A.

questions.question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced when the four arms P, Q, R, S satisfy
questions.explanation: At balance no current flows through the galvanometer, so the two midpoint potentials are equal. This gives the ratio condition P/Q=R/S.

questions.question: In a potentiometer, two cells have balancing lengths 40 cm and 60 cm on the same uniform wire. The ratio of their emfs E1/E2 is
questions.explanation: For the same potential gradient, emf is proportional to balancing length. Thus E1/E2=l1/l2=40/60=2/3.

questions.question: A uniform wire is stretched to twice its original length without loss of material or change in resistivity. Its resistance becomes
questions.explanation: Volume conservation gives A'=A/2 when L'=2L. Since R=rho L/A, R'=rho(2L)/(A/2)=4R.

questions.question: A current I flows through a wire of cross-sectional area A and carrier number density n. The drift speed magnitude is
questions.explanation: Current magnitude I=n e A v_d. Rearranging gives v_d=I/(neA).

questions.question: A source of emf E and internal resistance r supplies maximum power to a variable load R when
questions.explanation: The maximum power transfer condition for a resistive load is R=r. Then P=E^2R/(R+r)^2 is maximized.

questions.question: In the circuit shown, the bottom rail is ground. Ideal sources hold nodes S1 and S2 at +12 V and +6 V, respectively. Each of the four resistors shown is 2 ohm. Find the current through the resistor connecting nodes A and B, directed from A to B, in amperes.
questions.explanation: Use nodal analysis. At node A: (V_A-12)/2+(V_A-V_B)/2=0, so 2V_A-V_B=12. At node B: (V_B-6)/2+V_B/2+(V_B-V_A)/2=0, so -V_A+3V_B=6. Solving gives V_B=4.8 V and V_A=8.4 V. Therefore current from A to B is (V_A-V_B)/2=(8.4-4.8)/2=1.8 A.

questions.question: Find the equivalent resistance in ohms of 6 ohm and 3 ohm resistors connected in parallel.
questions.explanation: For parallel resistors, 1/R_eq=1/6+1/3=1/2, so R_eq=2 ohm.

questions.question: A 10 V cell with internal resistance 1 ohm is connected to a 4 ohm resistor. Find the current in amperes.
questions.explanation: Total circuit resistance is R+r=4+1=5 ohm. Current I=E/(R+r)=10/5=2 A.

questions.question: A wire has resistivity 2 x 10^-7 ohm m, length 5 m and area 1 x 10^-6 m^2. Find its resistance in ohms.
A 1 A current flows for 10 s. Using e=1.6 x 10^-19 C, find the number of electrons that pass a cross-section in units of 10^19 electrons, rounded to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: Charge transported Q=It=10 C. Number of electrons N=Q/e=10/(1.6 x 10^-19)=6.25 x 10^19. Rounded to the nearest integer in units of 10^19, this is 6.

questions.question: A 4 ohm resistor carries a current of 3 A. Find its power dissipation in watts.
A uniform potentiometer wire has a potential gradient of 0.04 V/cm. A cell balances at 75 cm. Find the cell emf in volts.
questions.explanation: The emf equals potential gradient times balancing length: E=0.04(75)=3 V.

questions.question: A charge q moves with speed v perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B. The magnitude of the magnetic force is
questions.explanation: The magnetic Lorentz-force magnitude is F=|q|vB sin(theta). For perpendicular velocity and field, sin(theta)=1, giving F=|q|vB.

questions.question: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the field. Its circular orbit radius is
questions.explanation: Magnetic force provides centripetal force: |q|vB=mv^2/r. Solving gives r=mv/(|q|B).

questions.question: A straight wire carrying current I lies perpendicular to magnetic field B over length L. The magnetic force magnitude is
questions.explanation: For a current element, F=BIL sin(theta). At 90 degrees, F=BIL.

questions.question: Two long parallel wires carry equal currents in the same direction. The magnetic force between them is
questions.explanation: Parallel currents in the same direction attract. Each wire experiences a magnetic field from the other that produces a force toward it.

questions.question: A circular loop of radius R carries current I. The magnetic field at its centre is
questions.explanation: Biot-Savart integration for a single circular loop gives B=mu_0 I/(2R) at its centre.

questions.question: A current loop has magnetic dipole moment m=IA. Its torque in uniform field B at angle theta between m and B is
questions.explanation: The torque is vector tau=m x B, so its magnitude is mB sin(theta).

questions.question: In a velocity selector with crossed perpendicular fields E and B, particles pass undeflected when their speed is
questions.explanation: For undeflected motion electric and magnetic force magnitudes balance: |q|E=|q|vB. Thus v=E/B.

questions.question: A rectangular current loop in a uniform magnetic field has zero net force but can have a nonzero
questions.explanation: For a closed loop in a uniform field, forces on opposite segments cancel, so net force is zero. Their lines of action can form a couple, producing torque tau=mB sin(theta).

questions.question: A proton has mass 1.67 x 10^-27 kg and charge 1.6 x 10^-19 C. It moves at 1.6 x 10^6 m/s perpendicular to a 1 T field. Find its orbit radius in centimetres, rounded to the nearest integer.
A 2 m wire carries 5 A perpendicular to a 0.4 T field. Find the magnetic force in newtons.
A circular coil has 10 turns, radius 0.2 m and current 2 A. Find the magnetic field at its centre in units of mu_0, i.e. find B/mu_0 in inverse metres times amperes.
A particle with charge magnitude 2 C moves at 3 m/s perpendicular to a 4 T field. Find the magnetic force in newtons.
Two parallel wires 1 m long carry 10 A and 20 A in the same direction and are separated by 0.1 m. Using mu_0/(2pi)=2 x 10^-7, find the force in units of 10^-4 N.
questions.explanation: F/L=(mu_0/(2pi))I1 I2/d. For L=1 m, F=(2 x 10^-7)(10)(20)/(0.1)=4 x 10^-4 N. In units of 10^-4 N, the answer is 4.

questions.question: A coil has magnetic moment 3 A m^2 in a 2 T uniform field, with moment perpendicular to the field. Find the torque in N m.
questions.explanation: Torque magnitude tau=mB sin90=3(2)=6 N m.

questions.question: An electron moves at 2 x 10^6 m/s perpendicular to B=0.5 T. Use |q|/m=1.76 x 10^11 C/kg. Find the cyclotron angular frequency in units of 10^11 rad/s to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: Cyclotron angular frequency omega=|q|B/m=(1.76 x 10^11)(0.5)=0.88 x 10^11 rad/s, which rounds to 1 when expressed in units of 10^11 rad/s.

questions.question: A wire of length 0.5 m carrying 4 A is parallel to a 3 T magnetic field. Find the magnetic force in newtons.
questions.explanation: F=BIL sin(theta). Here theta=0, so sin(theta)=0 and the magnetic force is zero.

questions.question: A coil of N turns experiences a uniform magnetic flux per turn changing from Phi_1 to Phi_2 in time Delta-t. The magnitude of average induced emf is
questions.explanation: Faraday's law gives |epsilon_avg|=N|Delta-Phi|/Delta-t. The sign is determined by Lenz's law, while the magnitude is the given positive ratio.

questions.question: A 0.5 m conducting rod moves at 4 m/s perpendicular to a uniform 2 T magnetic field, with rod, velocity and field mutually perpendicular. Its motional emf is
questions.explanation: Motional emf epsilon=BLv=(2)(0.5)(4)=4 V. The correct option is index 2.

questions.question: An inductor of 2 H carries current 3 A. The energy stored in its magnetic field is
questions.explanation: Inductor energy U=(1/2)LI^2=(1/2)(2)(9)=9 J.

questions.question: An RL circuit has resistance 10 ohm and inductance 2 H. Its time constant is
questions.explanation: The RL time constant is tau=L/R=2/10=0.2 s.

questions.question: A sinusoidal current has peak value I_0=10 A. Its rms value is
questions.explanation: For a sinusoidal current, I_rms=I_0/sqrt(2)=10/sqrt(2)=5sqrt(2) A.

questions.question: In a series RLC circuit at resonance, the impedance equals
questions.explanation: At resonance X_L=X_C, so the net reactance vanishes. The impedance is purely resistive, Z=R.

questions.question: The inductive reactance of a 0.1 H inductor at angular frequency 100 rad/s is
questions.explanation: Inductive reactance X_L=omega L=100(0.1)=10 ohm.

questions.question: An ideal capacitor is connected to a sinusoidal AC source. The average power dissipated in the capacitor over a full cycle is
questions.explanation: For an ideal capacitor current leads voltage by pi/2. Average power P=V_rms I_rms cos(phi), and cos(pi/2)=0.

questions.question: A 100-turn coil has flux per turn change by 0.02 Wb in 0.5 s. Find the magnitude of average induced emf in volts.
questions.explanation: Faraday's law gives epsilon=N Delta-Phi/Delta-t=100(0.02)/0.5=4 V.

questions.question: A 0.4 m rod moves at 5 m/s perpendicular to a 3 T field. Find the induced emf in volts.
questions.explanation: Motional emf is BLv=3(0.4)(5)=6 V.

questions.question: An inductor of 4 H carries 2 A. Find stored energy in joules.
An AC source has peak voltage 100 V. Find its rms voltage to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: V_rms=V_0/sqrt(2)=100/1.4142=70.71 V, rounding to 71 V.

questions.question: A 50 Hz AC supply drives a pure inductor of 0.1 H. Using pi=3.14, find its inductive reactance in ohms rounded to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: X_L=omega L=2pi f L=2(3.14)(50)(0.1)=31.4 ohm, which rounds to 31 ohm.

questions.question: A series RLC circuit has L=1 H and C=0.01 F. Find its resonant angular frequency in rad/s.
questions.explanation: Resonant angular frequency omega_0=1/sqrt(LC)=1/sqrt(1 x 0.01)=10 rad/s.

questions.question: A transformer has 500 primary turns and 100 secondary turns. If the primary rms voltage is 220 V, find the ideal secondary rms voltage in volts.
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer V_s/V_p=N_s/N_p=100/500=1/5. Thus V_s=220/5=44 V.

questions.question: An RL circuit has L=3 H and R=6 ohm. Find its time constant in units of 0.1 s.
questions.explanation: The RL time constant is tau=L/R=3/6=0.5 s. In units of 0.1 s, tau corresponds to 5.

questions.question: An electromagnetic wave travels in vacuum with electric-field amplitude E_0. Its magnetic-field amplitude B_0 is
questions.explanation: In a plane EM wave in vacuum, E_0/B_0=c. Therefore B_0=E_0/c.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly lists electromagnetic waves from lowest to highest frequency?
questions.explanation: Frequency increases in the sequence radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays. The second option gives the correct increasing order.

questions.question: A plane EM wave has electric-field amplitude 300 V/m in vacuum. Its magnetic-field amplitude is approximately
The average energy in a plane electromagnetic wave is shared between its electric and magnetic fields in the ratio
questions.explanation: In a plane EM wave in vacuum, E=cB. The electric energy density epsilon_0 E^2/2 equals magnetic energy density B^2/(2mu_0), since c^2=1/(epsilon_0 mu_0). Thus the ratio is 1:1.

questions.question: For an electromagnetic wave of frequency f in vacuum, its wavelength is
questions.explanation: All electromagnetic waves in vacuum travel at speed c. Since c=f lambda, wavelength lambda=c/f.

questions.question: A perfectly absorbing surface receives a normally incident EM wave of intensity I. Its radiation pressure is
questions.explanation: Momentum flux for complete absorption gives radiation pressure p=I/c. For perfect reflection the pressure would be 2I/c.

questions.question: Which statement about electromagnetic waves in vacuum is correct?
options: Their electric and magnetic fields are parallel
Their speed depends on frequency in vacuum
questions.explanation: In vacuum, electromagnetic waves are transverse: E and B are perpendicular to each other and to the propagation direction. Their speed is c independent of frequency.

questions.question: A source emits electromagnetic radiation at wavelength 600 nm in vacuum. Its frequency is approximately
questions.explanation: Frequency f=c/lambda=(3 x 10^8)/(600 x 10^-9)=5 x 10^14 Hz.

questions.question: An electromagnetic wave has wavelength 3 m in vacuum. Find its frequency in units of 10^8 Hz.
questions.explanation: f=c/lambda=(3 x 10^8)/3=1 x 10^8 Hz. The numerical value in units of 10^8 Hz is 1.

questions.question: A plane EM wave has E-field amplitude 600 V/m. Using c=3 x 10^8 m/s, find B-field amplitude in microtesla.
An electromagnetic wave has frequency 1.5 x 10^8 Hz in vacuum. Find its wavelength in metres.
A perfectly absorbing surface receives radiation of intensity 900 W/m^2. Using c=3 x 10^8 m/s, find radiation pressure in units of 10^-6 Pa.
questions.explanation: Pressure p=I/c=900/(3 x 10^8)=3 x 10^-6 Pa. The numerical value in units of 10^-6 Pa is 3.

questions.question: An EM wave in vacuum has magnetic amplitude 4 x 10^-7 T. Using c=3 x 10^8 m/s, find electric amplitude in V/m.
A radio wave has frequency 100 MHz. Find its wavelength in metres in vacuum.
questions.explanation: 100 MHz=1 x 10^8 Hz. Thus lambda=c/f=(3 x 10^8)/(1 x 10^8)=3 m.

questions.question: An isotropic source radiates power 120 W. Find intensity in W/m^2 at distance 1 m, rounded to the nearest integer. Use pi=3.14.
An EM wave has equal average energy density in its electric and magnetic fields, with total average energy density 8 J/m^3. Find the electric contribution in J/m^3.
questions.explanation: Electric and magnetic energy densities are equal in a plane EM wave. Each contributes half the total, so u_E=8/2=4 J/m^3.

questions.question: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. Using the Cartesian convention, the image is formed
questions.explanation: For a thin lens, 1/v-1/u=1/f. With u=-30 cm and f=+15 cm, 1/v+1/30=1/15, so 1/v=1/30 and v=+30 cm, on the opposite side.

questions.question: Two thin lenses of powers +2 D and -0.5 D are kept in contact. Their combined focal length is
questions.explanation: Powers add for thin lenses in contact: P=2-0.5=1.5 D. Focal length f=1/P=2/3 m, about 0.67 m, which is option index 2.

questions.question: A ray passes from glass (n=1.5) to air. The critical angle is
questions.explanation: For a denser-to-rarer boundary, sin(theta_c)=n_rarer/n_denser=1/1.5=2/3. Therefore theta_c=sin^-1(2/3).

questions.question: An object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror. The image is
questions.explanation: For a concave mirror, an object at C forms an image at C. The image is real, inverted and equal in size to the object.

questions.question: A medium has refractive index 1.5 relative to air. The speed of light in it is approximately
questions.explanation: Refractive index n=c/v, so v=c/n=(3 x 10^8)/1.5=2 x 10^8 m/s.

questions.question: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is used as a simple magnifier with the final image at infinity. Its angular magnification for a relaxed eye is approximately (near point D=25 cm)
questions.explanation: For a simple microscope with final image at infinity, magnifying power M=D/f=25/20=1.25.

questions.question: A prism has angle A=60 degrees and minimum deviation delta_m=40 degrees. Its refractive index is
questions.explanation: At minimum deviation, n=sin[(A+delta_m)/2]/sin(A/2)=sin50 degrees/sin30 degrees.

questions.question: A glass slab of thickness t and refractive index n is viewed normally from air. The apparent upward shift of its lower surface is
questions.explanation: Apparent depth is t/n. The shift is real depth minus apparent depth: t-t/n=t(1-1/n).

questions.question: A convex lens has focal length 10 cm. An object is placed 15 cm in front of it. Find the image distance in cm, using the thin-lens equation.
questions.explanation: Using 1/f=1/v-1/u with f=+10 cm and u=-15 cm gives 1/v=1/10-1/15=1/30, hence v=30 cm.

questions.question: Two lenses in contact have powers +4 D and +1 D. Find the combined focal length in centimetres.
questions.explanation: Combined power P=4+1=5 D. Focal length f=1/P=0.2 m=20 cm.

questions.question: A concave mirror has radius of curvature 40 cm. Find its focal-length magnitude in cm.
questions.explanation: For a spherical mirror, focal-length magnitude is |f|=R/2=40/2=20 cm.

questions.question: A glass of refractive index 1.5 is viewed from air. An object at real depth 12 cm appears at what depth in cm when viewed normally?
questions.explanation: Apparent depth=real depth/n=12/1.5=8 cm.

questions.question: A ray enters glass of refractive index 1.5 from air at incidence angle 30 degrees. If sin30=0.5, find 3 times the sine of the refraction angle.
questions.explanation: Snell law gives sin r=sin30/1.5=0.5/1.5=1/3. Therefore 3 sin r=1.

questions.question: An astronomical telescope in normal adjustment has objective focal length 100 cm and eyepiece focal length 5 cm. Find the magnitude of angular magnification.
questions.explanation: For normal adjustment, magnifying power magnitude M=f_o/f_e=100/5=20.

questions.question: A convex lens has focal length 25 cm. An object is placed 50 cm in front of it. Find the image distance in centimetres.
questions.explanation: Using 1/f=1/v-1/u with f=+25 cm and u=-50 cm gives 1/v=1/25-1/50=1/50. Hence v=+50 cm, on the opposite side of the lens.

questions.question: A ray travels in glass of refractive index 1.5 and reaches a glass-air boundary at the critical angle theta_c. Find 3 sin(theta_c).
questions.explanation: At the critical angle, sin(theta_c)=n_air/n_glass=1/1.5=2/3. Therefore 3 sin(theta_c)=2.

questions.question: In Young's double-slit experiment, wavelength is lambda, screen distance is D and slit separation is d. The fringe width is
questions.explanation: For small angles, fringe width beta=D lambda/d. It increases with wavelength and screen distance and decreases with slit separation.

questions.question: In a double-slit arrangement, the path difference at a point is lambda/4. The phase difference is
questions.explanation: Phase difference Delta-phi=2pi Delta-x/lambda=2pi(1/4)=pi/2.

questions.question: For single-slit Fraunhofer diffraction of slit width a, the first minimum occurs at angle theta satisfying
questions.explanation: Single-slit minima occur when a sin(theta)=m lambda for nonzero integer m. The first minimum has |m|=1.

questions.question: Unpolarized light of intensity I_0 passes through an ideal polarizer and then an analyzer at 60 degrees to the polarizer axis. The final intensity is
questions.explanation: The first polarizer transmits I_0/2. Malus's law through the analyzer gives I=(I_0/2)cos^2 60=(I_0/2)(1/4)=I_0/8.

questions.question: Two coherent waves of equal amplitude interfere. For constructive interference, the path difference must be
questions.explanation: Constructive interference requires phase difference 2m pi, equivalent to path difference Delta=m lambda for integer m.

questions.question: The resolving power of a diffraction grating generally increases when
options: the order is always reduced to zero
questions.explanation: For a grating, resolving power R=lambda/Delta-lambda=mN, where m is diffraction order and N is the number of illuminated lines. Increasing N increases resolving power.

questions.question: In Young's experiment, the entire apparatus is immersed in a liquid of refractive index n while geometry stays fixed. Fringe width becomes
questions.explanation: The wavelength in the medium is lambda'=lambda/n. Since beta=lambda D/d, the new fringe width is beta'=beta/n.

questions.question: A thin-film interference setup is illuminated normally. Ignoring phase reversals for this question, a bright condition for reflected rays with path difference 2nt is
questions.explanation: Under the stated assumption of no net phase reversal, constructive interference requires path difference 2nt=m lambda for integer m.

questions.question: In Young's double-slit experiment, lambda=600 nm, D=2 m and slit separation d=0.6 mm. Find fringe width in millimetres.
A path difference of 3lambda/2 produces a phase difference in units of pi radians. Enter the numerical value.
questions.explanation: Delta-phi=2pi(Delta-x/lambda)=2pi(3/2)=3pi. In units of pi radians the answer is 3.

questions.question: Unpolarized light of intensity 80 W/m^2 passes through one ideal polarizer. Find the transmitted intensity in W/m^2.
questions.explanation: An ideal polarizer transmits half the intensity of unpolarized incident light, so I=80/2=40 W/m^2.

questions.question: For a single slit of width 0.1 mm illuminated with wavelength 500 nm, estimate the angular position of the first minimum in units of 10^-3 radians, using the small-angle approximation.
questions.explanation: For the first minimum, theta approximately lambda/a=(500 x 10^-9)/(0.1 x 10^-3)=5 x 10^-3 rad. The numerical value in units of 10^-3 rad is 5.

questions.question: In Young's experiment, fringe width is 1.5 mm. If screen distance is doubled and slit separation is tripled, find the new fringe width in mm.
questions.explanation: beta is proportional to D/d. New beta=1.5(2/3)=1.0 mm.

questions.question: Two equal-amplitude coherent waves each have intensity 4 W/m^2. Find the maximum intensity in their interference pattern, in W/m^2.
questions.explanation: For two coherent waves, maximum intensity is (sqrt(I1)+sqrt(I2))^2. Here each intensity is 4 W/m^2, so I_max=(2+2)^2=16 W/m^2.

questions.question: Light has wavelength 500 nm in air and enters a medium of refractive index 1.25. Find its wavelength in the medium in nm.
questions.explanation: Frequency stays unchanged at a boundary, while wavelength scales as 1/n. Thus lambda'=500/1.25=400 nm.

questions.question: In Young's experiment, slit separation is 1 mm and the screen is 2 m away. If wavelength is 500 nm, find fringe width in millimetres.

chapter: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation

questions.question: In the photoelectric effect, the stopping potential is V_s and the incident frequency is f. Einstein's equation is
questions.explanation: Maximum photoelectron kinetic energy is K_max=hf-phi. A stopping potential satisfies eV_s=K_max, so eV_s=hf-phi for f above threshold.

questions.question: The threshold frequency of a metal is f_0. If incident light has frequency f_0/2, photoelectric emission
questions.explanation: A photon must have energy hf at least equal to work function phi=hf_0. If f<f_0, no single photon can release an electron, irrespective of intensity in the ordinary one-photon photoelectric model.

questions.question: The de Broglie wavelength of a nonrelativistic particle of momentum p is
questions.explanation: The de Broglie relation assigns wavelength lambda=h/p to a particle with momentum p.

questions.question: An electron accelerated from rest through potential V has de Broglie wavelength proportional to
questions.explanation: The electron gains kinetic energy eV=(1/2)mv^2, giving p=sqrt(2meV). Since lambda=h/p, lambda is proportional to 1/sqrt(V).

questions.question: For monochromatic light above threshold, increasing intensity while keeping frequency fixed increases the
options: maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons
number of emitted electrons per unit time, typically
questions.explanation: Photon energy hf is unchanged, so K_max=hf-phi and stopping potential stay fixed. Higher intensity means more photons per unit time and therefore typically higher photoelectric current.

questions.question: A photon has energy E. Its momentum magnitude is
questions.explanation: For a photon, E=pc. Therefore p=E/c.

questions.question: The work function of a metal is 2 eV. Light of photon energy 5 eV is incident. The maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons is
questions.explanation: Einstein's photoelectric equation gives K_max=E_photon-phi=5-2=3 eV.

questions.question: In a Compton-scattering experiment, the wavelength shift depends on the scattering angle and
options: electron rest mass and fundamental constants
questions.explanation: The Compton shift is Delta-lambda=(h/(m_e c))(1-cos theta). It depends on scattering angle and the electron mass, not on incident intensity or work function.

questions.question: A metal has work function 2 eV and is illuminated by photons of energy 7 eV. Find maximum photoelectron kinetic energy in eV.
questions.explanation: K_max=E_photon-phi=7-2=5 eV.

questions.question: An electron is accelerated from rest through 144 V. Using lambda in angstroms approximately 12.27/sqrt(V), find its de Broglie wavelength in angstroms rounded to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: lambda=12.27/sqrt(144)=12.27/12=1.0225 angstrom, which rounds to 1 angstrom.

questions.question: Light of wavelength 400 nm has photon energy approximately 1240/lambda(nm) eV. Find the photon energy in eV rounded to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: E=1240/400=3.1 eV, which rounds to 3 eV.

questions.question: A photon has energy 6 x 10^-19 J. Using c=3 x 10^8 m/s, find its momentum in units of 10^-27 kg m/s.
questions.explanation: p=E/c=(6 x 10^-19)/(3 x 10^8)=2 x 10^-27 kg m/s. The numerical value in the stated units is 2.

questions.question: A metal has threshold frequency 5 x 10^14 Hz. Light of frequency 8 x 10^14 Hz is incident. If h=6.6 x 10^-34 J s, find the maximum kinetic energy in units of 10^-20 J, rounded to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: K_max=h(f-f_0)=6.6 x 10^-34(3 x 10^14)=19.8 x 10^-20 J. In units of 10^-20 J this is 19.8, which rounds to 20.

questions.question: A particle has momentum 2 x 10^-24 kg m/s and Planck constant h=6.6 x 10^-34 J s. Find its de Broglie wavelength in picometres, rounded to the nearest integer.
A photoelectron has maximum kinetic energy 4 eV. Find the stopping potential magnitude in volts.
questions.explanation: eV_s=K_max. When K_max is expressed in eV, the numerical stopping potential in volts is the same number: 4 V.

questions.question: A photon of frequency 6 x 10^14 Hz has energy in units of h times 10^14 Hz. Enter the numerical coefficient.
questions.explanation: Photon energy is E=hf. With f=6 x 10^14 Hz, the coefficient multiplying h x 10^14 Hz is 6.

questions.question: In the Bohr model of hydrogen, the radius of the nth orbit is proportional to
questions.explanation: The Bohr radius formula is r_n=a_0 n^2/Z. For hydrogen Z=1, so r_n is proportional to n^2.

questions.question: The energy of the nth Bohr orbit in hydrogen is E_n=-13.6/n^2 eV. The energy needed to ionize hydrogen from n=2 is
questions.explanation: At n=2, E_2=-13.6/4=-3.4 eV. Ionization raises the energy to zero, so required energy is 3.4 eV.

questions.question: For a radioactive sample, after three half-lives the fraction of original nuclei remaining is
questions.explanation: After n half-lives the remaining fraction is (1/2)^n. At n=3 this is 1/8.

questions.question: The binding energy of a nucleus is primarily related to
options: its mass defect through E=Delta-m c^2
questions.explanation: Nuclear binding energy equals the mass defect times c^2: BE=Delta-m c^2, where Delta-m is the difference between separated-nucleon mass and actual nuclear mass.

questions.question: A hydrogen atom makes a transition from n=3 to n=2. The emitted photon belongs to the
questions.explanation: Transitions ending at n=2 form the Balmer series. The 3-to-2 transition is the first Balmer line.

questions.question: If the half-life of a radioactive isotope is T_1/2, its decay constant lambda is
questions.explanation: The decay law gives N=N_0 e^(-lambda t); at t=T_1/2, N/N_0=1/2, so lambda T_1/2=ln2 and lambda=ln2/T_1/2.

questions.question: The nucleus with the greatest binding energy per nucleon among typical stable nuclides lies near
questions.explanation: Binding energy per nucleon peaks near the iron-nickel region. This explains why fusion of light nuclei and fission of very heavy nuclei can release energy.

questions.question: A beta-minus decay changes the nuclear proton number Z and mass number A by
options: Z and A both increase by 1
questions.explanation: In beta-minus decay, a neutron converts to a proton plus an electron and antineutrino. Therefore Z increases by one while A remains unchanged.

questions.question: A hydrogen atom transitions from n=3 to n=1. Using E_n=-13.6/n^2 eV, find the emitted photon energy in eV rounded to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: E_1=-13.6 eV and E_3=-13.6/9=-1.511 eV. Photon energy is |E_1-E_3|=12.089 eV, rounding to 12 eV.

questions.question: A radioactive sample begins with 800 nuclei. How many remain after 3 half-lives?
questions.explanation: Each half-life halves the number. N=800(1/2)^3=800/8=100 nuclei.

questions.question: A nucleus has mass defect 0.2 u. Using 1 u c^2=931.5 MeV, find its binding energy in MeV rounded to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: Binding energy=Delta-m c^2=0.2(931.5)=186.3 MeV, rounding to 186 MeV.

questions.question: A nuclide has half-life 10 hours. What percentage of the original nuclei remains after 30 hours, rounded to the nearest integer?
questions.explanation: Thirty hours is three half-lives, so the remaining fraction is (1/2)^3=1/8=12.5%. Rounded to the nearest integer percentage, this is 13%.

questions.question: The mass number of a nucleus is 23 and its proton number is 11. Find the number of neutrons.
questions.explanation: Neutron number N=A-Z=23-11=12.

questions.question: In hydrogen, the energy of n=2 is -3.4 eV and of n=4 is -0.85 eV. Find the photon energy in eV for a transition from n=4 to n=2, rounded to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The photon energy equals the difference in bound-state energies: (-0.85)-(-3.4)=2.55 eV, which rounds to 3 eV.

questions.question: A sample's activity is 1600 decays/s initially. How many decays/s remain after four half-lives?
questions.explanation: Activity decays with the same half-life as the number of undecayed nuclei. A_4=A_0/2^4=1600/16=100 decays/s.

questions.question: A nucleus contains 8 protons and 9 neutrons. Find its mass number A.
questions.explanation: Mass number is total nucleons: A=Z+N=8+9=17.

questions.question: A pure semiconductor is doped with a pentavalent impurity. The resulting material is generally
options: p-type with holes as majority carriers
n-type with electrons as majority carriers
questions.explanation: A pentavalent donor supplies an extra electron to the conduction band. The semiconductor becomes n-type, with electrons as majority carriers.

questions.question: A p-n junction diode is forward biased when
options: p-side is connected to negative and n-side to positive
p-side is connected to positive and n-side to negative
both sides are connected to positive
the applied voltage is necessarily zero
questions.explanation: Forward bias connects p to the positive terminal and n to the negative terminal. This reduces the depletion barrier and permits substantial current.

questions.question: The output of an AND gate is 1 when
questions.explanation: An AND gate produces output 1 only when every input is 1. For two inputs, the truth table gives 1 only for (1,1).

questions.question: A Zener diode is commonly used in reverse breakdown to provide
questions.explanation: In its designed reverse-breakdown region, a Zener diode maintains an approximately constant voltage across changing current, enabling voltage regulation.

questions.question: In a common-emitter transistor in its active region, the approximate current relation is
questions.explanation: By charge conservation at the transistor terminals, emitter current equals collector current plus base current: I_E=I_C+I_B.

questions.question: A full-wave rectifier supplied by 50 Hz AC produces output pulsations at
questions.explanation: A full-wave rectifier uses both half-cycles, producing two output pulses per input cycle. Thus ripple frequency is 2f=100 Hz.

questions.question: The depletion region of a p-n junction contains
options: fixed ionized donor and acceptor ions with few mobile carriers
questions.explanation: Diffusion and recombination near the junction leave immobile ionized donors and acceptors. This space-charge region has very few mobile carriers and establishes the built-in field.

questions.question: Which logic gate produces output 1 only when its two inputs are different?
questions.explanation: The exclusive-OR gate is high for input pairs (0,1) and (1,0), and low for equal inputs.

questions.question: A transistor has collector current 9.8 mA and base current 0.2 mA. Find its emitter current in mA.

questions.question: A transistor has collector current 20 mA and base current 0.5 mA. Find the current gain beta=I_C/I_B.
questions.explanation: Current gain beta=I_C/I_B=20/0.5=40.

questions.question: An ideal diode is forward biased in series with a 1 kOhm resistor and a 5 V ideal source. Using a zero-drop diode model, find the current in mA.
questions.explanation: The ideal forward-biased diode drop is zero, so the resistor receives 5 V. Current I=V/R=5/1000=0.005 A=5 mA.

questions.question: An LED emits photons of wavelength 620 nm. Using E(eV)=1240/lambda(nm), find the photon energy in eV rounded to the nearest integer.

For a two-input NAND gate, find the output when both inputs are 1, encoded as 0 or 1.
questions.explanation: An AND gate returns 1 for inputs (1,1); NAND is its logical complement, so the output is 0.

questions.question: A transistor has alpha=0.98. Find beta=alpha/(1-alpha), rounded to the nearest integer.
A full-wave rectifier is supplied by 60 Hz AC. Find the output ripple frequency in Hz.
questions.explanation: Full-wave rectification produces two pulses per AC cycle, so ripple frequency=2(60)=120 Hz.
